title: Integral Noetherian separated curves have an ample invertible module
statement: Let $Y$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] scheme [def-pc-scheme] of topological Krull dimension $\dim Y=1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then some invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

proof.text: Choose a finite covering $Y=U_1\cup\cdots\cup U_r$ by nonempty affine opens (Y is quasi-compact, and is nonempty since integral; drop empty members). By [lem-sc-affine-complement-finite-on-integral-curve] each $Y\setminus U_i$ is finite.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09ND, proof, first two sentences

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sc-find-globally-generated] to the integral separated scheme $Y$, the nonempty affine open $U_i$, and its finite complement. Thus there are an invertible module $\mathcal L_i$ generated by global sections and a section $s_i$ with $(Y)_{s_i}=U_i$.
The pairs $(\mathcal L_i,s_i)$ cover $Y$ by affine principal opens. The quasi-compact criterion [lem-sc-enough-globally-generated-ample] therefore gives an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module.
